title: Getting started with dendroMixR
text: Fitting finite mixture model requires choosing number components kk. practice kk unknown, common overfit purpose: fit components believe really , try make sense result. Unfortunately, overfitted mixture models come real statistical cost. Parameter estimates overfitted mixing measure converge much slowly correctly-specified one — slowly n−1/8n^{-1/8} Gaussian mixtures — fit typically contains redundant, near-duplicate components hard interpret. dendroMixR implements method , , McKinley, Terhorst, Nguyen, “Dendrogram mixing measures: Hierarchical clustering model selection finite mixture models” (Biometrika, 2025). idea take single overfitted fit repeatedly merge two similar components (“atoms”), producing nested sequence mixing measures k,k−1,…,1k, k-1, \dots, 1 components — much like agglomerative hierarchical clustering, applied mixture atoms rather data points. paper shows merging procedure recovers fast, root-nn convergence rate true number components, even though starting overfitted fit converged slowly, without ever re-fitting model. vignette shows two core functions action: dendrogram_mixing() performs merging returns hierarchical clustering object (hc), sequence intermediate mixing measures (Gs), merge history (merge_pair). plot_dendrogram_mixing() visualizes result dendrogram, one parameter dimension shown time.

title: Getting started with dendroMixR
text: working simulated data, helps see dendrogram_mixing() small, hand-built mixing measure mechanics clear. six atoms one dimension, arranged atoms 1-2, 3-4, 5-6 close together (EM fit produced redundant near-duplicate components near three “true” locations roughly −2-2, 00, 33): dmm_toy$hc$height gives dissimilarity merge happened. atoms 1-2, 3-4, 5-6 near-duplicates, expect first merges happen much smaller height later ones join genuinely distinct components: heights jump roughly two orders magnitude third fourth merges — exactly pattern ’d want, since first three merges clean redundant atoms last two join real, separated components.
code: ps_toy     <- c(0.05, 0.30, 0.05, 0.30, 0.15, 0.15) thetas_toy <- c(-2.1, -1.9, 0.05, -0.05, 3.0, 3.2)  dmm_toy <- dendrogram_mixing(ps_toy, thetas_toy) str(dmm_toy, max.level = 1) #> List of 3 #>  $ hc        :List of 5 #>   ..- attr(*, "class")= chr "hclust" #>  $ Gs        :List of 6 #>  $ merge_pair: int [1:5, 1:2] 3 1 3 1 1 4 2 4 2 2 dmm_toy$hc$height #> [1] 0.0004285714 0.0017142857 0.0030000000 0.6270089286 3.4994169643

title: Getting started with dendroMixR
text: component variance known shared across components (strongly identifiable case), dendrogram_mixing() needs weights means: sigmas = NULL. case also covers common practice overfitting via hard-clustering method kk-means, implicitly assumes equal, fixed variance across clusters. simulate data well-separated 3-component 1-D Gaussian mixture unit variance, deliberately overfit k=8k = 8 clusters: Now merge overfitted fit dendrogram_mixing(): dmm1$Gs holds mixing measure every level tree, k=8k = 8 atoms k=1k = 1. Cutting true k0=3k_0 = 3 (Gs[[k_over - k0 + 1]]) recovers weights means close truth (0.3/0.4/0.3 −4,0,5-4, 0, 5), even though re-fitting took place: plot_dendrogram_mixing() visualizes merge sequence. column points one level tree (kk atoms 1); tracing gray branches left right shows atoms combine height:
code: n   <- 2000 ps0 <- c(0.3, 0.4, 0.3) mu0 <- c(-4, 0, 5) k0  <- 3  z <- sample(k0, n, replace = TRUE, prob = ps0) x  <- rnorm(n, mu0[z], sd = 1)  k_over <- 8 km <- kmeans(x, centers = k_over, nstart = 20) ps_over    <- as.numeric(table(km$cluster)) / n theta_over <- as.numeric(km$centers) dmm1 <- dendrogram_mixing(ps_over, theta_over) dmm1$hc$height #> [1] 0.07689073 0.08837710 0.17687009 0.22175558 0.23793065 2.95811472 9.08888408 merged3 <- dmm1$Gs[[k_over - k0 + 1]] merged3$ps #> [1] 0.2835 0.3275 0.3890 merged3$thetas #> [1]  5.0022964 -3.9013129  0.1775128 plot_dendrogram_mixing(dmm1, main = "Strong identifiability: 1D merge")

title: Getting started with dendroMixR
text: Location-scale Gaussian mixtures — mean covariance estimated — weakly identifiable known especially slow convergence overfitted. Pass sigmas argument (list covariance matrices multivariate data, numeric vector variances 1-D) use weak-identifiability merge rule. simulate 2-D data three Gaussians different covariance structures fit overfitted k=8k=8 Gaussian mixture mclust: Cutting k0=3k_0 = 3 recovers parameters close truth: dendrogram_mixing() returns standard hclust object $hc, familiar tools like cutree() work directly — recovering 8 overfitted components belong 3 underlying clusters: parameters multivariate , plot_dendrogram_mixing() takes dim argument choose coordinate display:
code: library(mclust) #> Package 'mclust' version 6.1.3 #> Type 'citation("mclust")' for citing this R package in publications.  n <- 1500 ps0  <- c(1/3, 1/3, 1/3) mus0 <- matrix(c( 2, 1,                    0, 6,                   -2, 1), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE) sigmas0 <- list(   matrix(c(0.50,  0.30,  0.30, 1.00), 2, 2),   matrix(c(0.50, -0.10, -0.10, 0.10), 2, 2),   matrix(c(0.25,  0.30,  0.30, 2.00), 2, 2) ) k0 <- 3  z <- sample(k0, n, replace = TRUE, prob = ps0) x <- matrix(0, n, 2) for (i in seq_len(n)) x[i, ] <- MASS::mvrnorm(1, mus0[z[i], ], sigmas0[[z[i]]])  k_over <- 8 fit <- Mclust(x, G = k_over, modelNames = "VVV", verbose = FALSE)  ps_over     <- fit$parameters$pro mus_over    <- t(fit$parameters$mean) sigmas_over <- lapply(seq_len(k_over), function(j) fit$parameters$variance$sigma[, , j]) dmm2 <- dendrogram_mixing(ps_over, mus_over, sigmas_over) dmm2$hc$height #> [1] 0.03087893 0.07070912 0.07414885 0.15825751 0.35408244 2.77082574 6.64579123 merged3_weak <- dmm2$Gs[[k_over - k0 + 1]] merged3_weak$ps #> [1] 0.3519913 0.3160262 0.3319826 matrix(merged3_weak$thetas, ncol = 2) #>             [,1]     [,2] #> [1,]  0.03990841 5.981140 #> [2,] -2.02639862 0.949602 #> [3,]  1.98373254 1.023402 cutree(dmm2$hc, k = 3) #> 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 8  #> 1 1 2 3 1 3 2 2 plot_dendrogram_mixing(dmm2, dim = 1, main = "Weak identifiability: dim 1") plot_dendrogram_mixing(dmm2, dim = 2, main = "Weak identifiability: dim 2")
